learningObjectives: Apply method overriding and polymorphism in Java.
Use abstract classes and interfaces to define reusable contracts.

activities.title: Inheritance Map
activities.instruction: Explore the relationship between parent and child classes.

content.concept: Inheritance allows a subclass to extend a superclass and reuse accessible fields and methods. The subclass can also add new behavior or override inherited methods.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The superclass representing common animal behavior.
A method inherited by compatible subclasses.
Behavior specific to the Dog subclass.
The Dog object can use the inherited eat method.

activities.title: Method Override Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a method override.

content.concept: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides a compatible implementation of an inherited instance method. The subclass implementation can then be selected when the object is used polymorphically.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Annotation indicating that the method is intended to override an inherited method.
The subclass providing the new implementation.
The subclass-specific implementation of the method.

activities.title: Polymorphism Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the behavior produced by each parent-type reference.

content.concept: With runtime polymorphism, a superclass reference can refer to a subclass object. When an overridden instance method is called, Java selects the implementation associated with the actual object at runtime.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Animal a = new Dog(); a.sound() → Dog's overridden sound()
Animal a = new Cat(); a.sound() → Cat's overridden sound()
config.answer: Animal a = new Dog(); a.sound() → Dog's overridden sound()

activities.title: Abstraction Builder
activities.instruction: Build an abstraction that defines required behavior without exposing implementation details.

content.concept: Abstraction focuses on what an object must do rather than how it does it. Abstract classes and interfaces can define contracts that concrete classes implement.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
